text:
alex: quick spike idea — add a tiny "smokeprofile" job to CI that auto-captures nsys/perfetto traces for PRs touching runtime kernels. target: kernel selection + KV cache hot paths.

maria: sounds useful but storage/cost is my concern. run on every PR?

alex: not every PR. trigger when files under eng/runtime/** or models/kernels/** change. Keep the trace very small: 5 short requests, 2 phases (cold + warmed), 20–30s capture windows.

jin: how do we decide to keep a trace? we can't archive everything.

alex: plan: always upload a small summary JSON (~1–2KB). only persist full trace if (a) size < 50MB OR (b) perf-bot flags a regression against baseline.

sanjay: perf-bot can compute metrics from the trace: total kernel time, top-3 kernels (by time), avg latency, kernel selection variance. if any metric regresses >10% we keep the full artifact and create a diff-dashboard entry.

maria: also important — short runs might miss cold KV cache behavior. we should do two phases: first run cold (no warmup), then run 10 requests to populate KV cache and capture warmed behavior. label artifacts accordingly.

alex: agree. rough GH Actions snippet I'll include in the PR:
```yaml
name: smokeprofile-trace
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'eng/runtime/**'
      - 'models/kernels/**'
jobs:
  trace-smoke:
    runs-on: gpu-small
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: setup docker
        run: docker pull ghcr.io/redwood/runtime-perf:smoke
      - name: capture trace
        run: |\
          docker run --gpus all --rm -v $GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/w ghcr.io/redwood/runtime-perf:smoke \
            /bin/bash -c "./capture_trace.sh --profile nsys --mode smoke --cold-requests 5 --warm-requests 10 --duration 25 --out /w/artifacts/trace.ns"
      - name: upload artifact summary
        run: ./scripts/compute_trace_summary.py /w/artifacts/trace.ns > /w/artifacts/summary.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: trace-summary
          path: artifacts/summary.json
```

kai: two small suggestions — 1) compress traces with zstd before upload, it's usually 3–5x smaller; 2) generate a tiny flamegraph PNG (thumbnail) and upload that so reviewers can get immediate insight without downloading huge files.

jin: also add deterministic flags: set SEED and log kernel-selection decisions to runtime logs. kernel scheduling can be non-deterministic across runs and makes diffs noisy. capture runtime-config.json with model name, quantization, sequence length, cuda/driver info.

perf-bot: Uploaded summary to s3://redwood-perf/summaries/1945678901-summary.json — metrics: total_kernel_time_ms=132.4, top_kernels=[GEMM(62%), SOFTMAX(18%), LAYERNORM(7%)], avg_lat_ms=24.8. (this is a simulated message).

alex: excellent. next steps: I'll open the PR with the action + small capture container. sanjay — can you own the baseline storage and the minimal dashboard for the first month? we'll avoid auto-triage until we have ~100 runs.

sanjay: I can own that. I'll add a lightweight page that plots baseline vs latest and links to s3 artifacts. we'll also surface a short regression email to eng-runtime if we see >15% degradation sustained across 3 runs.

maria: sounds good. one more ops ask — add a retention policy: summaries forever, full traces for 90 days unless pinned. compress and strip NVTX names except top-5 kernels to reduce size.

alex: noted, will include in PR description. thanks all :thumbsup:

kai: tiny note — for partners/private deployments we should gate trace upload behind a flag. avoid PII or customer input in traces. mask prompts and only capture tokenized lengths.

alex: yep, capture harness will use synthetic prompts and mask any user data.

maria: love it — eager to see the first smoke traces.

alex: I'll tag you all on the PR once it's ready.
